source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 574 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-574.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 574 was established by Ordinance No. 24223, passed by the Dallas City Council on April 12, 2000. Ordinance No. 24223 amended Ordinance No. 19455, Chapter 51A of the Dallas City Code, as amended. (Ord. Nos. 19455; 24223; 25163)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-574.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 574 is established on property located on the northeast side of Highland Road, northwest of Ferguson Road. The size of PD 574 is approximately 4.588 acres. (Ord. Nos. 24223; 25163)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-574.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all code references are to Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered to be a residential zoning district. (Ord. Nos. 24223; 25163)

SEC. 51P-574.103.1. EXHIBIT.

The following exhibit is incorporated into this article: Exhibit 574A: conceptual plan. (Ord. 31053)

SEC. 51P-574.103.2. CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the conceptual plan (Exhibit 574A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the conceptual plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 31053)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-574.104. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

(a) For single family uses and accessory uses, a final plat may serve as the development plan. If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the development plan, the text of this article controls.

(b) For all other uses, a development plan must be approved by the city plan commission before issuance of any building permit. (Ord. Nos. 24223; 25163; 31053)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-574.105. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

The only main uses permitted are those main uses permitted in the R-5(A) Single Family District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the R-5(A) Single Family District, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the R-5(A) Single Family District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this district only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the R-5(A) Single Family District is subject to DIR in this district; etc. (Ord. Nos. 24223; 25163; 31053)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-574.106. ACCESSORY USES.

(a) As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific types of accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations contained in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217.

(b) The following accessory uses are not permitted in this planned development district:

-- Accessory helistop. -- Accessory medical/infectious waste incinerator. -- Accessory outside display of merchandise. -- Accessory outside sales. -- Accessory pathological waste incinerator. -- Private stable.

(c) An accessory community center (private) is permitted by right. (Ord. Nos. 24223; 25163; 31053)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-574.107. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. If there is a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls.)

(a) Front yard. Minimum front yard is 10 feet for single family structures, and 20 feet for all other permitted structures.

(b) Side and rear yard. Minimum side yard is 10 feet. Minimum rear yard setback is five feet for single family structures, and 10 feet for all other permitted structures.

(c) Density. Maximum number of dwelling units permitted on the Property is 35.

(d) Floor area. No maximum floor area ratio.

(e) Height. Maximum structure height is 36 feet.

(f) Lot coverage. Maximum lot coverage is 70 percent for residential structures and 25 percent for nonresidential structures. For a shared access development, the entire Property is considered one lot for the calculation of lot coverage and the shared access area is included for the calculation of lot coverage.

(g) Lot size. Minimum lot area for residential use is 2,250 square feet. For a shared access development, the shared access area is included in the calculation of lot size.

(h) Stories. No maximum number of stories. (Ord. Nos. 24223; 25163; 31053)

sections.title: Fence
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-574.108. FENCE.

For a single family use, a six-foot-high solid fence is permitted along Highland Road. (Ord. Nos. 24223; 25163; 31053)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-574.109. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) For a single family use, two off-street parking spaces are required per lot.

(b) For all other uses, consult the use regulations in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(c) Consult the off-street parking and loading regulations (Division 51A-4.300 et seq.) for information regarding off-street parking and loading generally. (Ord. Nos. 24223; 25163; 31053)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-574.110. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. Nos. 24223; 25163)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-574.111. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(b) A minimum five-foot wide landscaped parkway must be provided along Highland Road. The landscaped parkway must be in compliance with Section 51A-10.125(b)(1)(B).

(c) Plant material must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. Nos. 24223; 25163; 31053)

sections.title: Tree Preservation And Mitigation
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-574.112. TREE PRESERVATION AND MITIGATION.

Tree preservation must be provided as outlined in Article X, except as follows:

(1) Tree removal applications may be approved by the building official prior to the submission of an application for a building permit on the Property.

(2) A tree survey that complies with the requirements of Article X must be submitted in conjunction with a preliminary plat for the Property.

(3) Mitigation of protected trees must be completed in accordance with the following time frame: 50 percent of the total required caliper inches must be completed prior to the final inspection for the single family structure which will result in the completion of the 9th single family structure on the Property; 75 percent of the total required caliper inches must be completed prior to the final inspection for the single family structure which will result in the completion of the 13th single family structure on the Property; 100 percent of the total required caliper inches must be completed prior to the final inspection of the last single family structure constructed on the Property. (Ord. Nos. 24223; 25163)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-574.113. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts contained in Article VII. (Ord. Nos. 24223; 25163)

sections.title: Access
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-574.114. ACCESS.

For a single family use, ingress and egress to the Property must be provided as shown on the conceptual plan. For a shared access development, a maximum of 35 residential lots may be served by one ingress and egress point. (Ord. Nos. 24223; 25163; 31053)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-574.116. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) Roll-over or mountable curbs are allowed, subject to design and construction approval by the director of public works and transportation.

(b) Individual garage doors must be architecturally compatible with the main building.

(c) A minimum five-foot wide sidewalk must be provided along Highland Road.

(d) For a shared access development, a minimum three-foot sidewalk that connects each of the shared access drives to the common area is required.

(e) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(f) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 24223; 25163; 26102; 31053)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-574.117. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the director of public works and transportation.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit or certificate of occupancy for a use in this planned development district until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. Nos. 24223; 25163; 26102)
